claim: The sink-path overvoltage protection cannot be set high enough for the 24 V adapter. VOVP4RCP is programmable only up to 24 V. Above that, GATE_VBUS (the internal VBUS-to-PPHV switch) is turned off. The adapter's normal 25.2 V, and any 24 V adapter running above nominal, sits above every possible setting. PPHV then stays off, so the BQ25756 never gets an input and the port cannot charge from the adapter. The limit comes from the EEPROM configuration (U402/U502), and no value in that memory covers 25.2 V. This is a separate limit from the 22 V recommended-VBUS issue the engineer already reported: it is a hard functional cut-off, not a rating margin.

The required '26.5 V input overvoltage cut-off' does not cut anything off. The ACUV/ACOV divider hangs on PPHV, which sits behind the TPS25751D switch, not on VBUS. ACOV only stops the converter. J401, D401, U401.VBUS, U405 C_CC/VBIAS, C406 and C450 stay connected to the adapter at whatever voltage it delivers. Nothing in the circuit holds the VBUS net to its declared max_v of 26.5 V, so that declaration is an assumption about the adapter, not something the board enforces (question 8). Also, PPHV is opened by the TPS25751D OVP at 24 V or below (F1), so ACOV at 26.5 V can never trip. Worst-case ACOV trip is 1.206 V x (163.6k+50.4k+9.9k)/9.9k = 27.3 V, which is above the TVS2700's 27 V standoff.

evidence.quote: When VACOV rises above VREF_ACOV, the device automatically stops the converter and the PG pin pulls high.

claim: The new CC protector is not rated for a CC-to-VBUS short at this adapter's voltage. Its short-to-VBUS tolerance on C_CCx is specified at 21.5 V max. The datasheet (p.10) describes its high-voltage ESD clamp as '21.5V DC tolerant'. The 28 V abs-max the gate checked does not show this. The requirement is a CC short to 25.2-26.5 V DC. A plain 24 V adapter cannot be told to detach through a forced PD detach, so the short is continuous. The C_CC ESD clamp is then held above its DC-tolerant voltage indefinitely. The part's title is '20V SPR Port Protector'. An EPR-rated (28 V or higher) CC protector is needed.

evidence.quote: Short-to-VBUS tolerance on the CC pins Type C Cable, place a 30-Ω load on 21.5 V

claim: The VBIAS capacitor kept from the old design is a 0.1u 50V 0402 (CL05B104KB54PNC). The TPD4S201 footnote requires at least a 63 VDC rating and recommends 100 V. The effective value must stay within 0.04-0.14 uF after voltage derating. In a CC short, VBIAS charges to about the 25 V adapter voltage, with ringing clamped near 28 V (p.15). A 0402 50 V X7R at 25 V bias is near or below the 0.04 uF minimum. Per p.15, more derating means more ringing in the short-to-VBUS event.

evidence.quote: The VBIAS pin requires a minimum 63-VDC rated capacitor.

claim: The capacitance behind the internal PPHV switch is about 225 uF nominal: 4 x 22u, 2 x 68u polymer tantalum, 1u, 0.1u, 0.1u through the 5 mOhm RAC. The TPS25751D recommends at most 100 uF on PPHV. When the switch closes on a 25.2 V adapter, it must charge this bank from 0 V. That is about 5.7 mC and 1.6 times the stored energy of the old 20 V case, with no external inrush limiting. The switch's SOA (Figure 6-6) at 25 V source-to-source has not been checked.

The gate never checked the PPHV pin, because the TPS25751D limits file has no PPHV row (review packet, section 1). PPHV is declared at 26.5 V. Its recommended maximum is 22 V (p.8) and its abs max is 28 V (p.7), the same exceedance as the VBUS pin, but on a pin nobody reported. Add PPHV abs-max and recommended rows so the gate flags it.

A plain 24 V adapter hot-plugs straight to 24 V. A PD source starts at 5 V and changes voltage slowly. That plug-in edge, plus cable ringing, is far faster than the 2.5 V/us the Maxinmicro sheet allows before the flat-clamp TVS starts conducting. So the TVS conducts on every plug-in, close to its 27 V standoff. The sheet warns that regular fast swings overheat the device. Confirm on the bench with the real adapter and cable.

evidence.quote: it is recommended to keep the slew rate of any input signal on the TVSXX00DRVR below 2.5 V/μs at room temperature
